explanations: There is no defect. sealSave draws a fresh 12-byte random IV per write, so GCM nonces are never reused under a key. The auth tag is stored and checked with setAuthTag before final(), and the AAD binds each blob to its playerId and slot, so swapping rows between players fails authentication. The key version byte lets old blobs decrypt after rotation, and needsRewrap re-encrypts them under the active key. The database connection uses TLS with a pinned CA and rejectUnauthorized: true, and the HTTPS server sets a TLSv1.2 minimum.

aadFor(playerId, slot) is passed to setAAD on both encrypt and decrypt. The blob was sealed with A's AAD, so decrypting with B's AAD makes decipher.final() throw, and that becomes SaveDecryptError. The key is the same, but GCM also authenticates the AAD. The version byte is unchanged, and needsRewrap runs only after decryption has succeeded.

openSave picks the key from the version byte in the blob (2), so decryption works. needsRewrap then sees 2 !== activeVersion and calls write, which seals the blob again with key 3. No bulk migration is needed, it never tries key 3 on a version-2 blob, and the row does not stay on version 2 after it is read.

ssl.ca supplies the trusted CA bundle and rejectUnauthorized: true makes the driver refuse certificates that don't validate against it, so a man-in-the-middle can't pose as the database. Accepting any certificate is what rejectUnauthorized: false would do. Encryption at rest is done separately by sealSave, and there is no plaintext fallback.
